title: Local rational collection of opposite root products
statement:
Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional rational vector space and $R\subset V\setminus\{0\}$ a reduced crystallographic root system spanning $V$, with coroot functionals $\bar c_\alpha$ and weight lattice $P=\{v\in V:\bar c_\alpha(v)\in\mathbf Z\text{ for every }\alpha\in R\}$ in the conventions of [lem-sfb-root-datum-lattice-embedding]. Let $\mathfrak g,\mathfrak h,h_\delta,e_\alpha,\rho,W,\Omega,\Lambda$ satisfy the Chevalley-basis and faithful-representation conditions of [lem-sfb-chevalley-admissible-representation]: $\mathfrak g$ is split semisimple over $\mathbf Q$, $\rho$ is faithful on finite-dimensional $W$, the nonzero weight spaces $W_\lambda$ have weights $\Omega\subset P$ with $\mathbf Z\Omega=P$, and the full lattice $\Lambda=\bigoplus_{\lambda\in\Omega}(\Lambda\cap W_\lambda)$ is stable under every $D_{\alpha,m}=\rho(e_\alpha)^m/m!$, with $\rho(e_\alpha)$ nilpotent. Fix a simple-root base $\Delta$, meaning a subset $\Delta\subseteq R$ which is a basis of $V$ such that every root has integral coordinates in $\Delta$ all nonnegative or all nonpositive. Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], $W_F=\Lambda\otimes_{\mathbf Z}F$, and $T=D_F(P)=\operatorname{Spec}F[P]$, where $F[P]$ has basis $e^\lambda$, multiplication $e^\lambda e^\mu=e^{\lambda+\mu}$, comultiplication $e^\lambda\mapsto e^\lambda\otimes e^\lambda$, counit $e^\lambda\mapsto1$, and antipode $e^\lambda\mapsto e^{-\lambda}$. Embed $T$ in $\operatorname{GL}(W_F)$ by its weight characters on the summands $(\Lambda\cap W_\lambda)\otimes F$. Define the finite polynomial matrices $x_\alpha(a)=\sum_{m\geq0}(D_{\alpha,m}\otimes1)a^m$ for every commutative $F$-algebra. Group schemes and closed subgroups have the meanings of [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup], and $\mathbf G_a,\mathbf G_m$ those of [def-sc-gm-ga].  Put $R^+=R\cap\sum_{\delta\in\Delta}\mathbf Z_{\geq0}\delta$, $N=|R^+|$, and fix any order on $R^+$ refining nondecreasing height (the sum of the simple-root coefficients). Write $p_+(b)=\prod_{\beta\in R^+}x_\beta(b_\beta)$ and $p_-(a)=\prod_{\beta\in R^+}x_{-\beta}(a_\beta)$, using this order. There exist a polynomial $d\in F[a_\beta,b_\beta:\beta\in R^+]$ with $d(0,0)=1$, morphisms $A,B:D(d)\to\mathbf A_F^N$, and a morphism $h:D(d)\to T$, such that the identity of matrix-valued morphisms
$$p_+(b)p_-(a)=p_-(A(a,b))\,h(a,b)\,p_+(B(a,b))$$
holds on the principal open $D(d)=\operatorname{Spec}F[a,b,1/d]$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. At $(a,b)=(0,0)$ one has $A=B=0$ and $h=1$. In particular this is an identity after evaluation in any commutative $F$-algebra in which $d(a,b)$ is a unit, including nonreduced algebras and characteristics two and three. No generated group, its reductivity, or an open-immersion property is assumed or asserted. For $R=\varnothing$ one may take $d=1$, the unique maps $A,B$, and $h=1$.

proof.text: Write $\Delta=\{\delta_1,\ldots,\delta_r\}$ and $H_i=h_{\delta_i}$. The simple coroots are a rational basis and generate the coroot lattice by [lem-sfb-root-base-rational-integral-spans], applied to the root-coroot pairing; hence the hypotheses for [lem-sfb-kostant-integral-pbw] hold for the given Chevalley basis. In its integral enveloping algebra $U_{\mathbf Z}$ denote the ordered PBW basis by $Q_{u,v,w}=\prod_\beta e_{-\beta}^{(u_\beta)}\prod_i\binom{H_i}{v_i}\prod_\beta e_\beta^{(w_\beta)}$. Use exactly the two orders in the item. Give the rational enveloping algebra the coproduct $\mathcal D(e_\gamma)=e_\gamma\otimes1+1\otimes e_\gamma$. This respects $xy-yx=[x,y]$, since the two tensor factors commute. The binomial identities give $\mathcal D(e_\gamma^{(m)})=\sum_{j+k=m}e_\gamma^{(j)}\otimes e_\gamma^{(k)}$ and $\mathcal D\binom{H_i}{m}=\sum_{j+k=m}\binom{H_i}{j}\otimes\binom{H_i}{k}$. Thus it preserves $U_{\mathbf Z}$ and $\mathcal D(Q_I)=\sum_{J+K=I}Q_J\otimes Q_K$, where $I=(u,v,w)$. These are finite equalities in the free integral PBW bases; no reduction of factorial denominators in $F$ has occurred.

source.place: Section 23h, equation (153), Theorem 23.72 and Notes, printed pp.510--511; agent expansion of the omitted local collection argument using integral PBW and block Gauss uniqueness.

proof.text: For this coefficient calculation only, write $\mathbf Z[[a,b]]$ for the ring of all formal series in the $2N$ parameters, with multiplication by the finite coefficient-convolution sums. In $U_{\mathbf Z}[[a,b]]$ put $G=\prod_\beta(\sum_{m\ge0}e_\beta^{(m)}b_\beta^m)\prod_\beta(\sum_{m\ge0}e_{-\beta}^{(m)}a_\beta^m)$. Every parameter coefficient is an element of $U_{\mathbf Z}$, so it has a finite PBW expansion. Write $G=\sum_I c_IQ_I$ coefficientwise. Each root exponential is group-like by the divided-power coproduct from step 1; therefore $\mathcal D(G)=G\otimes G$, where the right side multiplies series with the same parameters. Comparing the coefficient of $Q_J\otimes Q_K$ yields $c_{J+K}=c_Jc_K$. The augmentation taking each Lie generator to zero gives $c_0=1$. Set $A^\wedge_\beta=c_{(1_\beta,0,0)}$, $z_i=c_{(0,1_i,0)}$, and $B^\wedge_\beta=c_{(0,0,1_\beta)}$. They have zero constant term because $G(0)=1$. Repeatedly using the displayed recurrence gives $c_{u,v,w}=\prod_\beta(A^\wedge_\beta)^{u_\beta}\prod_i z_i^{v_i}\prod_\beta(B^\wedge_\beta)^{w_\beta}$. This is a coefficient comparison, rather than a smoothness or group-generation argument.

source.place: Section 23h, equation (153), Theorem 23.72 and Notes, printed pp.510--511; agent expansion of the omitted local collection argument using integral PBW and block Gauss uniqueness.

proof.text: Reinsert the coefficients from step 2 into the ordered PBW expansion. It gives the formal identity $G=(\prod_\beta\sum_m e_{-\beta}^{(m)}(A^\wedge_\beta)^m)(\prod_i\sum_m\binom{H_i}{m}z_i^m)(\prod_\beta\sum_m e_\beta^{(m)}(B^\wedge_\beta)^m)$. All products and substitutions are legitimate coefficientwise: each substituted parameter has zero constant term, so any fixed parameter degree involves only finitely many indices. The representation extends to $U_{\mathbf Q}$ by [lem-sfb-kostant-integral-pbw]. Its $U_{\mathbf Z}$ action preserves $\Lambda$: the generators are precisely the divided powers assumed integral in the item, as recorded in [lem-sfb-chevalley-admissible-representation]. On a weight summand $\Lambda\cap W_\lambda$, $\binom{H_i}{m}$ acts by the integer $\binom{\bar c_{\delta_i}(\lambda)}{m}$. For negative integers $-k$, integrality follows from $\binom{-k}{m}=(-1)^m\binom{k+m-1}{m}$. Consequently the middle factor acts by $\prod_i(1+z_i)^{\bar c_{\delta_i}(\lambda)}$. The map $\lambda\mapsto\prod_i(1+z_i)^{\bar c_{\delta_i}(\lambda)}$ is a homomorphism $P\to\mathbf Z[[a,b]]^\times$; it defines a point $h^\wedge$ of the weight-character torus. Applying the integral matrices and then the coefficient map $\mathbf Z\to F$ gives $p_+(b)p_-(a)=p_-(A^\wedge)h^\wedge p_+(B^\wedge)$ over $F[[a,b]]$. Nilpotence makes each represented root exponential finite. This construction works without inverting any integer in $F$.

source.place: Section 23h, equation (153), Theorem 23.72 and Notes, printed pp.510--511; agent expansion of the omitted local collection argument using integral PBW and block Gauss uniqueness.

proof.text: Choose a rational functional $q$ positive on the simple roots and separating the finitely many distinct weights. Such a choice exists: in the dual coordinates of the simple-root basis, the positive rational orthant is not contained in any of the finitely many hyperplanes $q(\lambda-\mu)=0$; equivalently evaluate these finitely many nonzero rational polynomials at a sufficiently large positive integer using coordinates $(1,M,\ldots,M^{r-1})$. Order the weight blocks by decreasing $q$. By [lem-sfb-chevalley-unipotent-polynomial-coordinates], $p_-$ and $p_+$ identify their affine coordinate spaces with closed subgroup schemes $U_-\subset L$ and $U_+\subset U$ of the corresponding block lower and upper unitriangular groups. The torus $T$ lies in the block diagonal group $D$. Its inclusion there is closed: in a weight basis, the coordinate functions given by a diagonal entry and the corresponding inverse-matrix entry restrict to $e^\lambda,e^{-\lambda}$. Since $\mathbf Z\Omega=P$, these functions generate $F[P]$ as an $F$-algebra. Hence the coordinate map $F[D]\to F[P]$ is surjective, which explicitly gives a closed immersion. In particular $U_-\times T\times U_+$ is closed inside $L\times D\times U$.

source.place: Section 23h, equation (153), Theorem 23.72 and Notes, printed pp.510--511; agent expansion of the omitted local collection argument using integral PBW and block Gauss uniqueness.

proof.text: Set $g(a,b)=p_+(b)p_-(a)$. Apply [lem-sfb-block-gauss-scheme-chart] with $E=W_F$ and the nonzero blocks $E_i=(\Lambda\cap W_{\lambda_i})\otimes F$ in the weight order of step 4, choosing a basis in each block. Each block is nonzero because its lattice has rank $\dim_{\mathbf Q}W_{\lambda_i}>0$. Let $\Delta_j(g)$ be the determinant of the leading block on $\bigoplus_{i\leq j}E_i$ and set $d=\prod_j\Delta_j(g)$. The matrices $x_\alpha$ have polynomial entries and inverse $x_\alpha(-a)$: the finite exponential identity over $\mathbf Q$ is an equality of integral polynomial matrices on $\Lambda$, hence remains valid after base change. Thus $g$ maps to $\operatorname{GL}(E)$ and $g(0)=1$, so $d(0)=1$. In $S=F[a,b,1/d]$, every $\Delta_j(g)$ is a unit: its inverse is $d^{-1}\prod_{k\ne j}\Delta_k(g)$. The cited chart's inverse therefore gives morphisms $l:D(d)\to L$, $t:D(d)\to D$, $u:D(d)\to U$ with $g=ltu$, unique functorially over every commutative $F$-algebra. The map $S\to\widehat S=F[[a,b]]$ is injective: $d$ has constant term one and is a formal unit, and a fraction $f/d^n$ mapping to zero has zero polynomial numerator after multiplication by $d^n$.

source.place: Section 23h, equation (153), Theorem 23.72 and Notes, printed pp.510--511; agent expansion of the omitted local collection argument using integral PBW and block Gauss uniqueness.

proof.text: Over the commutative $F$-algebra $\widehat S=F[[a,b]]$, the formal factors of step 3 belong to $L(\widehat S),D(\widehat S),U(\widehat S)$ by step 4. Uniqueness in [lem-sfb-block-gauss-scheme-chart] therefore identifies $(l,t,u)$ over $\widehat S$ with $(p_-(A^\wedge),h^\wedge,p_+(B^\wedge))$. Each equation defining the closed subschemes $U_-\subset L$, $T\subset D$, $U_+\subset U$ consequently has zero image in $\widehat S$ under the respective coordinate maps. Injectivity of $S\to\widehat S$ makes its image zero already in $S$. Those coordinate maps therefore factor through the defining quotient rings, giving $l\in U_-(S)$, $t\in T(S)$, $u\in U_+(S)$ as scheme-theoretic assertions. Compose $l,u$ with the inverses of the closed-immersion coordinate identifications $p_\pm:\mathbf A^N\simeq U_\pm$ from [lem-sfb-chevalley-unipotent-polynomial-coordinates]. These are the required morphisms $A,B:D(d)\to\mathbf A^N$; put $h=t$. The identity $g=ltu$ becomes precisely the displayed identity $p_+(b)p_-(a)=p_-(A(a,b))h(a,b)p_+(B(a,b))$ over $S$.

source.place: Section 23h, equation (153), Theorem 23.72 and Notes, printed pp.510--511; agent expansion of the omitted local collection argument using integral PBW and block Gauss uniqueness.

proof.text: The injection into formal series shows that the constant terms of $A,B,h$ are those of $A^\wedge,B^\wedge,h^\wedge$, namely $0,0,1$ by steps 2--3. Alternatively Gauss uniqueness at $g(0)=1$ gives identity factors, whose $p_\pm$ coordinates are zero. For any commutative $F$-algebra $C$ and parameters with $d(a,b)\in C^\times$, polynomial evaluation extends uniquely to $S\to C$ by $f/d^n\mapsto f(a,b)d(a,b)^{-n}$. Applying this ring map to the matrix identity proves it over $C$, including nilpotent elements and characteristics two and three. If $R$ is empty, then $V=0$, $P=0$, $N=0$, $T=1$, and all root products are $1$; take $d=1$ and the unique affine coordinate maps. No ambient generated group or reductivity assertion was used.
